sources.news_title: Trump tells US troops ‘victory at hand’ over Iran
sources.text:
Washington: US President Donald Trump told US troops that the United States had “victory at hand” over Iran and was giving Tehran “every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives,” but expressed doubt that Iranian leaders would accept the opportunity.
Trump made the remarks during Thanksgiving calls to service members from his Mar-a-Lago residence in Palm Beach, Florida, where he was joined by first lady Melania Trump.
“We have victory at hand. It’s going to be whenever, sort of, whatever I want it to be,” Trump said during the first call, to an Army unit involved in Operation Epic Fury.
“We’re giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives. But I’m not sure if they are going to take advantage of that,” he said.
Trump also reiterated that Iran would never have a nuclear weapon, presenting that objective as central to the troops’ mission.
Later, speaking to an Air Force lieutenant colonel based in Saudi Arabia and operating F-16 fighter aircraft, Trump asked whether the officer was encountering a “much tamer enemy.”
The officer agreed and said his assessment was that Iran was running short of resources. The exchange, recorded in the pool report, did not provide details supporting that assessment.
Trump also spoke with personnel aboard the USS Portland, deployed to the Indo-Pacific region, and praised the naval blockade of Iran. He described it as the most successful in naval history, without providing a basis for the comparison.
Asked by an Air Force service member about his vision for future US relations in the Middle East, Trump said he wanted peace in the region and again ruled out allowing Iran to obtain a nuclear weapon.
The calls came a day after Trump met NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte at Mar-a-Lago.
A joint statement published by NATO on Thursday identified the Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict in Iran as the main subjects of that meeting. It said the leaders also discussed avoiding an expansion of the war in Ukraine, pursuing a peaceful resolution and increasing defense spending and industrial investment.
During the troop calls, Trump credited himself with securing NATO allies’ commitment to higher defense spending.
Under the alliance’s 2025 Hague summit declaration, members committed to spending 5 per cent of gross domestic product annually by 2035 on defence and related security needs. That includes at least 3.5 per cent for core defense requirements and up to 1.5 per cent for broader spending, including infrastructure and resilience. The target concerns national expenditure, rather than payments to NATO.
After completing calls that also included the Marine Corps, Space Force and Coast Guard, Trump answered reporters’ questions. He said his discussion with Rutte had focused mostly on Russia and Ukraine.
Trump expressed his belief that Russian President Vladimir Putin wanted the war to end and said NATO also wanted an end to the fighting. He did not announce a new agreement in those remarks.

sources.news_title: Trump says US has victory at hand in Iran war, offers Tehran chance for deal - The Tribune
sources.text:
Florida [US], November 27 (ANI): US President Donald Trump has said that America has "victory at hand" in its war on Iran, while indicating that Washington is allowing Tehran to reach an agreement to prevent further loss of life.
Speaking during a Thanksgiving call alongside First Lady Melania Trump, with US military personnel from his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thursday (local time), Trump said that the timing of the victory would be his decision, while expressing uncertainty over whether Iran would accept the opportunity for a deal.
Trump said, “We have victory at hand [in Iran]. It will happen whenever I want it to happen. We are trying to be nice. We are giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives, but I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that. Many people question why - are they crazy? Maybe they are.”
Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, on Thursday, in a series of messages on his official Telegram channel, in an interview with IRNA, said that Tehran's immediate focus was on strengthening the country's resilience against external pressures, while maintaining trade routes and meeting domestic requirements.
“Our main focus is on the country's resilience and helping to increase resilience against the pressures that enemies apply through various means,” Araghchi said.
He added that his colleagues, particularly those working in neighbouring countries, were working continuously to meet Iran's requirements and ensure that trade routes remained open.
“My colleagues, especially in neighbouring countries, are working around the clock to meet the country's needs, keep trade routes open, and take any other action that helps meet the country's needs. The goal is for the enemies to know that it is not possible to surround Iran and they cannot surround our country,” he said.
Addressing the possibility of negotiations, Araghchi maintained that diplomacy remained part of Tehran's approach, but said that countering external pressure was currently a more important priority.
“Negotiation is part of our work, and we have not forgotten it, and we are pursuing it; but in the current situation, there is also a more important mission, and that is to discourage the enemies from the sanctions and pressures they are imposing on our country. The path of negotiations also has its own mechanism and is pursued under the supervision of the Supreme National Security Council,” he said.
The Iranian Foreign Minister further confirmed that mediation efforts by Qatar and Pakistan were continuing, with both countries conveying proposals and suggestions.
“The Qatari and Pakistani mediators are also still active, putting forward and conveying ideas and suggestions. This is a normal process. If there are specific ideas or views that could pave the way, these are being considered,” Araghchi said.
Meanwhile, in an interview with Shahrara News, reposted on his official Telegram account, Araghchi accused Israel of making statements aimed at creating an atmosphere conducive to another conflict and drawing the United States into a war with Iran.
“In recent days, the Zionist regime has resorted to every lie to create a war atmosphere and attribute the blame to Iran. It has become quite clear that every day they make a strange statement and a big claim; claims that perhaps only naive people, who are usually found in the West itself, will believe. This is the atmosphere-building that the Zionists are doing so that they can once again bring America into the war,” he said.
He also referred to the recent US elections, claiming that their results reflected growing awareness among American voters about the perceived prioritisation of Israeli interests over those of the United States.
“The results of the recent elections clearly showed the extent to which American public opinion has realised and become aware that the interests of the Zionist regime are taking precedence over American interests; this is not something I am saying, but it has also been raised in America itself, and even the President and Vice President of the United States have mentioned this issue,” Araghchi said.
Reiterating Tehran's position on the conflict, he said Iran viewed American and Israeli policies as aligned, while maintaining that the country remained prepared for both defence and diplomacy.
“We do not see any difference between the Zionist regime and American policies in general. We are fully prepared to defend ourselves, and we know very well how to defend ourselves. We are also prepared for diplomacy, and if our demands are respected and met, we are ready to move forward on this path,” he added.
The statements come amid contrasting positions from Washington and Tehran, with Trump projecting an impending US victory while offering Iran an opportunity for negotiations, and Araghchi reiterating Iran's preparedness to defend itself alongside its willingness to pursue diplomacy. (ANI)

sources.news_title: Trump says US has "victory at hand" in Iran war, offers Tehran chance for deal
Fury as Trump tells deployed troops their war ends 'whenever I want it to be'
sources.text:
President Donald Trump offered a pep talk to troops serving overseas but instead delivered a message that left people fuming.
On Thursday, Trump spoke with deployed service members over the phone to mark Thanksgiving, and remarked that he can decide when their deployment ends.
"You're going to continue that deployment, and we have victory at hand," Trump said. "It's going to be—whenever sort of—whenever I want it to be, to be honest."
The remark landed as troops spent the holiday far from their families, and it quickly drew a flood of responses from people who found it callous.
"The dude just cannot stop being an a—," blasted former Army official and combat veteran Chad Scott in a post on X. "That's all he is, all the f— time. They're like, 'Hey, say something nice about the troops on Thanksgiving,' and instead, it's just an endless stream of verbal vomit."
"Just the message service members want to hear on Thanksgiving while away from their families fighting his war of choice," added Wu Tang is for the Children, a popular political commentary account on X.
"Such a gifted orator," joked author Brittany Belle.
"Wow. Another historic quote for the Miami Presidential Library Resort and Spa," quipped independent journalist Patrick Howley.
Trump and first lady Melania Trump made the calls from Mar-a-Lago, and those on the line included members of a unit that took part in Operation Epic Fury, the U.S. military campaign against Iran, CBS News reported.
The deployment comment wasn't the only awkward moment, as Trump also told Marine Lt. Col. Matthew Andrews, "If you ever leave, we're gonna replace you very easily."
"What a guy," reacted the X account for The Tennessee Holler, a progressive news site.
Trump told the New York Post earlier this week that operations against Iran are funded through January, while admitting the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress could tie his hands.

sources.news_title: Trump tells US service members victory over Iran is ‘at hand’
Trump tells troops victory over Iran is at hand, questions Tehran's willingness to deal
sources.text:
US President Donald Trump declared Thursday that the United States was on the verge of victory over Iran, while expressing doubts about the Islamic Republic's willingness to reach an agreement to end the war.
Speaking to American service members deployed overseas on the occasion of Thanksgiving, Trump indicated that the timing of the campaign's conclusion remained in his hands.
"The First Lady and I joined millions of Americans this holiday to pray for your safety and success, and you're going to continue that deployment. And we have victory at hand. It's going to be sort of whenever I want it to be, to be honest," Trump told the troops.
The President stressed that his administration was seeking to avoid further bloodshed by offering Tehran opportunities to resolve the conflict through negotiations.
"We're trying to be nice. We're giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives. But I'm not sure if they are going to take advantage of that. Some people question why. Are they crazy? Maybe they are," Trump stated.
Speaking to reporters later, Trump was asked whether he had spoken to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in recent days, and said that he had.
He then commented on the prospects of further strikes on Iran and said, “We're trying to give them a chance to be smart. They have no military. Their military is decimated. Their air force is wiped out. Their navy is wiped out. Their anti-aircraft is wiped out."
He added, “They haven't been able to do anything with their nuclear sites that we wiped out. But if we did anything, we would hit Pickaxe [Mountain]. I mean, we can tell them because they can't do anything about it."
The remarks came two days after Trump revealed in an Oval Office interview with The New York Post that American military operations against Iran were funded through January, while acknowledging that the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress could constrain his ability to pursue further military action.
“I don’t know how they could do that politically, because we have a win. We can put that war to bed anytime we want."
Asked whether the opportunity to launch additional strikes against Iran was narrowing, Trump responded: “I find it hard to believe that they take a win and make it into a loss because that’s what would happen - Yeah, but up until really the end of January, pretty much, you know, we’re funded."
During the same interview, Trump described Israel's objective of toppling the Iranian regime as “probably doable," but clarified that his administration's priority was eliminating the Iranian nuclear threat rather than pursuing regime change.
“I just don’t want them to have a nuclear weapon. I was never for or against regime change, that was never a criteria for me," he said.
Trump had previously indicated in an interview with Fox News correspondent Trey Yingst on Sunday that he was inclined to authorize another major military campaign against Iran after the beginning of 2027 if negotiations proved unsuccessful.
While confirming that indirect contacts with Tehran were ongoing, Trump described Iranian negotiators as "professional tap dancers," adding, "They talk all the time. All they do is talk, but it's all BS."
Tehran, meanwhile, has intensified its threats against Washington as the American naval blockade continues.
On Wednesday, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesman Hossein Mohebbi claimed that mounting financial costs and exhaustion among American troops would eventually compel Washington to abandon the blockade and withdraw its forces from the region.
Mohebbi insisted that Iran's armed forces remained fully equipped and prepared for further confrontation, citing their capabilities over the preceding 15 to 16 months.
Iranian Deputy Parliament Speaker Hamidreza Hajibabaei separately threatened the security of oil exports from other countries in the region as a means of countering Washington's economic pressure.
A day earlier, Iranian National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei vowed to break the American blockade and respond forcefully to any additional military operations against Iran.
Rezaei dismissed the blockade as “delusional and futile," asserting that it would ultimately meet the same fate as what he characterized as Washington's failed military campaign.

sources.news_title: Trump says US giving Iran 'every opportunity' to reach agreement, doubts they will agree
sources.text:
US President Donald Trump told American service members on Thursday evening that “we have victory at hand,” while saying his administration was still giving Iran a chance to reach a deal. Speaking from Mar-a-Lago, Florida, during a series of Thanksgiving calls with US troops, Trump said Washington was giving Tehran “every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives.”
“But I’m not sure if they are going to take advantage of that,” he added. “Some people question why. Are they crazy? Maybe they are.”
After his Thanksgiving calls with US service members, Trump was asked whether he had spoken with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. “Yes, I have,” he replied. But when the reporter asked how he was preparing to work with Israel’s next leadership, Trump turned to Iran. He said Iran’s military had been severely weakened and that the US was still giving Tehran a chance to reach a deal. He did not directly address the question about Israel’s leadership transition.
“We’re trying to give them a chance to be smart,” Trump said of Iran. He claimed that its air force, navy, and air defenses had been wiped out and that Tehran had been unable to resume work at the nuclear sites the US had struck.
“We would absolutely hit Pickaxe Mountain, but we haven’t seen any real activity there,” he said, naming the site as a target if the US were to strike again. He did not announce a decision to launch another attack.
Trump says US does not need Middle East oil
Earlier, a US Air Force service member asked Trump how he saw America’s future relationships in the Middle East. Trump said the US did not need the region’s oil but had long been there to protect Israel and other countries in the region.
“What we do need is we need peace in the Middle East,” he said. He argued that Iran would use a nuclear weapon against Israel and other countries in the region if it acquired one. “That’s why we’re not going to let them have a nuclear weapon,” he said.
Trump also said he had discussed Iran in his recent talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. “Both of them want to see the Iran deal, and I think they’re helping me in that regard,” he told reporters.
He played down the significance of any intelligence Russia or China might be sharing with Tehran.
US launched 150 missiles to stop enemy action in Strait, Trump claims
Speaking to Marines stationed in the United Arab Emirates, Trump said the US had launched 150 missiles “to stop enemy missiles and drones from striking commercial ships in the Strait.” He did not specify the period covered by that figure, which could not be independently verified.
In a separate call with the crew of the USS Portland, Trump said the ship had spent more than 150 consecutive days at sea this year and had helped enforce the blockade on Iran, which he called the most successful in naval history.
When a member of the Coast Guard asked how he had spent Thanksgiving, Trump replied, “I’m working on a little project. It’s called Iran.”
The calls also turned to holiday favorites: Trump picked Florida over his native New York for Thanksgiving and pumpkin pie with vanilla ice cream for dessert. First Lady Melania Trump opted for apple pie, also with vanilla ice cream.
